title_ar: سماحة العلامة الشيخ الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء يخطب في الحجاج الموريتانيين بعرفات
title_en: The Eminent Scholar Sheikh al-Dedew, President of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, Preaches to the Mauritanian Pilgrims at Arafat
body_ar: ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء سلسلة محاضرات في موسم الحج لهذا العام 1433هـ، حيث ألقى خطبة عرفة في مخيم الحجاج الموريتانيين يوم التاسع من ذي الحجة 1433هـ الموافق 25 أكتوبر 2012م، حيث وعظ الحجاج وذكرهم ببعض فوائد الحج وأحكامه، ومنة الله عليهم بأن وفقهم لتأدية مناسكه، وقد تناولت الخطبة النقاط التالية: • سرد لأعمال الحج حسب ما روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم. • تذكر مشاهد القيامة والعرض على الله. • نصائح في كيفية الاستفادة من يوم عرفة. • علامات الحج المبرور. • تذكر مآسي الأمة. وقام الشيخ خلال أيام الحج بعدة محاضرات في إطار الأنشطة الدعوية التي يقوم بها كل عام في موسم الحج، من ضمنها: محاضرة ألقاها في منىً بعنوان: "ثمرة الحج المبرور"، ومحاضرة أخرى في مخيم البعثة الموريتانية في منىً. كما استضافته قناة الجزيرة في أول أيام التشريق -يوم السبت- في نشرة الساعة العاشرة صباحا بالتوقيت العالمي، كما استضافته أيضا قناة المجد في نفس اليوم في حدود الساعة الثالثة عصرا بالتوقيت العالمي. هذا بالإضافة إلى مناشط أخرى دعوية دأب الشيخ على القيام بها كل سنة في موسم الحج والعمرة. لمشاهدة خطبة عرفة لهذا العام 1433هـ إضغط هنا.
body_en:
Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, delivered a series of lectures in the hajj season of this year, 1433 AH. He delivered the Arafat sermon (khuṭbah) in the camp of the Mauritanian pilgrims on the ninth of Dhu al-Hijjah 1433 AH, corresponding to 25 October 2012, exhorting the pilgrims and reminding them of some of the benefits of hajj and its rulings, and of God's favour upon them in granting them success in performing its rites. The sermon took up the following points:

- A recounting of the acts of hajj according to what has been narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
- Calling to mind the scenes of the Resurrection and the presentation before God.
- Counsels on how to benefit from the Day of Arafat.
- The signs of an accepted hajj (al-ḥajj al-mabrūr).
- Calling to mind the tragedies of the community.

During the days of hajj the Sheikh gave several lectures, as part of the missionary activities he undertakes every year in the hajj season, among them a lecture he delivered at Mina entitled "The Fruit of the Accepted Hajj", and another lecture in the camp of the Mauritanian mission at Mina.

The Al Jazeera channel also hosted him on the first of the days of tashrīq — Saturday — in the ten o'clock bulletin, universal time; and the al-Majd channel likewise hosted him on the same day at around three in the afternoon, universal time. This is in addition to other missionary activities which the Sheikh has made a practice of undertaking every year in the hajj and lesser pilgrimage (ʿumrah) season.

*[Site link: "To watch the Arafat sermon for this year, 1433 AH, click here."]*

flags.context: علامات الحج المبرور ... ثمرة الحج المبرور
flags.note: mabrūr is the term of the well-known report that 'the accepted hajj has no reward but Paradise'. The scholars differ over what it names: a hajj God has accepted, a hajj untainted by sin or ostentation, or one whose effect shows in the pilgrim's subsequent conduct — and the Sheikh's own heading, 'the signs of al-ḥajj al-mabrūr', presupposes one of these without the record saying which. 'Accepted' is used as the least committal. The term is not in the glossary and should be added.

flags.arabic: وذكرهم ببعض فوائد الحج وأحكامه ... سرد لأعمال الحج حسب ما روي عن النبي
flags.context: the sermon's content, as headings only
options: render the headings and supply nothing
supply the rulings from the Maliki school
flags.note: Style guide section 10. The record says the Sheikh reminded the pilgrims of the rulings of hajj and recounted its acts as narrated from the Prophet, and gives not a single ruling or act. A reader arriving at a page headed with an Arafat sermon will expect the sermon; the corpus holds five headings and a dead link. Nothing may be supplied, least of all rulings on the rites, where the schools differ.

options: the first of the days of tashrīq — Saturday
the first day after Eid — Saturday
flags.note: The ayyām al-tashrīq are the three days following the Day of Sacrifice, spent at Mina. The term is left transliterated with no gloss because any gloss would state a ruling-bearing definition the record does not give; the corpus's fiqh material will need a settled rendering. Note also the internal date check: 9 Dhu al-Hijjah 1433 fell on Thursday 25 October 2012, making the first day of tashrīq Saturday 27 October, which is consistent.

flags.context: the last heading of the Arafat sermon
options: calling to mind the tragedies of the community
recalling the calamities of the ummah
flags.note: The one heading in the sermon that is not about the rites. In October 2012 'the tragedies of the community' would have been heard as Syria, Palestine, Myanmar and the aftermath of the film episode — all of which appear in neighbouring records in this slice. The English keeps the phrase as general as the Arabic and supplies none of that; it is recorded here so that a reviewer with the recording can see what was meant.

translator_notes: A news-desk summary of the Sheikh's activity during the hajj of 1433. The Arafat sermon itself exists only as the recording the record points to.
The CMS timestamp, 1 November 2012, is a bulk-upload date; the sermon was delivered on 9 Dhu al-Hijjah 1433 / 25 October 2012.
'منىً' is Mina, the valley east of Mecca where pilgrims stay during the days of tashrīq. The source writes it with tanwīn on the alif maqṣūrah, which English does not carry.
'مناشط' is a plural of manshaṭ used in Gulf and North African journalese for activities or events; rendered 'activities'.
